newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks battered by profit-taking, futures.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks battered by profit-taking, futures.

text.p: Tokyo stocks finished lamely on Wednesday, shedding all of their gains accumulated on Tuesday, brokers said. They added the market was battered by profit-taking as well as intermittent selling bouts of futures, with the market direction unclear and domestic investors quiet.
At the end of the day, the Nikkei 225 average had lost 226.99 points, or 1.07 percent, ending at 20,979.44. Its December futures were 140 points lower at 21,060.
"Small-lot selling munched away gains and once in a while futures-linked selling would add downward pressure," Harushige Kobayashi, Yamaichi Securities deputy general manager, said.

Amidst a lack of energy to deal in large-capital issues, speculative issues gathered attention, brokers said. Sumitomo Seika Chemicals Co Ltd, the second most heavily traded issue with 8.314 million shares, rose 15 yen to 899 yen.
Major gains were the communications and precision instrument sectors. The leading retreaters were pulp/paper, railway/bus, fisheries, warehouses and services.
Olympic Sports was suspended from OTC trade. It said later that it was going to apply for bankruptcy. The OTC index stood at 1,461.95, down 3.17 points, or 0.22 percent.
